posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
The first thing I would suggest is checking if it is the computer and not your game.
For example if a computer has a rather aggressive setting for its antivirus, it will continuously scan the game (website) while the browser is active, and that will cause additional lag.
And different computers have different reserves for lag due to different hardware and different background programs.
Then it can depend on the internet connection. Depending on where you live and where said friend lives, you can have different connectivity to your server.
In my opinion it is not impossible but rather unlikely that the effects are caused by your game.

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
yes and no
the problem is that "lag" is a summary of dozens of different causes. That creates some problems in two ways:
first you need to identify the cause of the lag before you can optimize that specific cause.
second sometimes the lag is caused from opposites and you can only do the best compromise instead of finding a solution.

posts.author: TheAM-Dol
posts.body:
Hey, I actually made a copy-pasta finally!
RPG Maker is a single-core/single-threaded, and MV is a 32 bit application (MZ is 64 bit, whoop), but both woefully under utilizes the GPU.
Doesn't matter how much ram or how many cores/threads your super CPU has as the application cannot take advantage of that. Everything is running on a single thread, so things can quickly bottleneck. Because of its single-core/single-thread preference, RM likes fast CPUs, not multi-core CPUs.
If it changes system to system, then it sounds like a hardware issue, and I would assume that it may be memory related; either the RAM is slow or single channel RAM, or the system may be using a slower drive, such as an old hard drive or a SSD without a DRAM cache (these type of SSDs tend to have a really high burst performance like most SSDs, but once saturated in transfer, some of the cheaper ones can slow to a crawl - slower than a hard drive).
I didn't read your full post, it's a lot to go through. I did see someone mention the reddit post about editing the garbage collection.
This is a bad idea. Garbage collection is RM's memory management. I
will
concede and say by default the garbage collection is rather aggressive for desktop purposes, but for mobile purposes it makes sense.
Really be careful following people's advice on prodding around files when you or the person posting doesn't know what they are talking about.
The garbage collection is going to clear unused references in memory every x number of frames.
When you tried setting it to 1, that means every frame it clears unused references in memory, this is likely going to cause the game to stutter more.
When you set it to 12,000 frames this is 3 minutes and 20 seconds. Every time you load a map new references are created and old ones are released. If you can walk across a map in 3 minutes, you are basically storing 2 maps worth of data in RAM when you only need 1 - and keep in mind, usually the largest RAM spike is loading new scenes.. While the default garbage collector I think is a little bit too aggressive, I would probably make it wait no more than 10 seconds between clean ups.
Other things that could be related are preloaders. Preloaders keep things in reference in the memory. Depending on how much you are preloading it could potentially cause problems (again, depending on the user's hardware).
If I missed specific bits of information you have pointed out, let me know. To me, this doesn't sound necessarily like a game problem but more of a hardware problem, but you could always take steps to improve the game's performance.

posts.author: Eternidade_1
posts.body:
In my opinion, you are experiencing lag due to ABS. If it works smoothly at 60 fps, it should continue to work at this demo standard.
I think there are plugins that improve ABS performance.
The drop in frame rate may be due to reading game data as variables, which is normal.
Avoid automatic map executions, parallel processes, and try to reduce the size of the game maps, reduce the number of events on the maps.
And use common event calls or scripts to read and end the process.
By doing this, you can have significant gains in your game systems.
